script.base: LV is a 3-point home favorite in a dome, total 40.5, implied LV 21.8 / MIA 18.8. Most likely a competitive, lower-play game LV leads late but not by a blowout: LV leans run with Ashton Jeanty to protect a small lead, MIA stays close enough that this is not garbage time, and neither offense is priced to explode.
script.flip1: LV jumps ahead early by more than a field goal, clocks it with Jeanty carries, and MIA abandons the run so De'Von Achane's rush yards stall while LV stays short and run-heavy with Brock Bowers out.
script.flip2: MIA hangs around or leads, both sides throw more than a 40.5 total implies, Jeanty's late carry pile-up never comes, and receiving (Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, Achane, Greg Dulcich) matters more than rushing.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Jeanty finished under 50.5 rush yards. LV fell behind or stayed pass-heavy without Bowers, the clock-killing carries never showed up, and Tucker or Nailor (boom games of 43-49 and 47-49 in the last four) ate the target void instead. The 128-yard game made last four look like an over trend while the 17-game median sits on 50.5, so the number was never soft. No run-defense charting means MIA may have been a bad front we could not see. Prior-season logs may not be this offense. With no price, even a right read could have been short odds.

Do not pair with MIA skill overs or a total over.
